app.title: GTsR: solvent removal from MOF crystal structures, with a stability check
app.summary: A person uploads a crystal structure file and looks at the raw structure in a 3D viewer, along with its formula and atom count. They choose which solvents to remove (free only, or all) and a probability threshold, then run a graph neural network that splits the structure into framework and solvent. They look at the cleaned framework or the removed solvent in a second viewer, which also lists the solvent molecules as SMILES strings. They download the cleaned structure file and can run a model that predicts whether the framework stays stable once activated.

task.text: Strip solvent molecules from a porous framework crystal structure with a learned model, check that the cleaned framework will stay stable once activated, and save it for simulation.

data.text: A single crystal structure in CIF format: the atoms and the unit cell of a porous framework, possibly with guest solvent molecules inside
data.item: one crystal structure file (CIF) of a metal-organic framework

stage.text: cleaning experimental crystal structures before molecular simulation or screening

mechanism.text: An uploaded structure is drawn in an interactive 3D molecular viewer with display options. Running the model shows a second viewer of the result that toggles between framework and removed solvent. The result is kept only while the input file and model choice stay the same.

field.text: machine-learned structure cleaning of metal-organic frameworks in computational materials chemistry

workflow.name: clean a single structure with a model and check the result

steps.here: Upload one CIF file (up to the uploader limit). It is parsed with ASE and rewritten as a normalized unit cell.
A 3D viewer with the unit cell drawn, options for style (ball and stick, stick, space filling, line), element labels and rotation, and metric cards for chemical formula and atom count

steps.step: compute a value from the data
steps.here: Choose the solvent type (Free Only or All, which picks the model checkpoint) and a threshold from 0 to 1, then press Start Cleaning Your MOF to split the structure into framework and solvent
The Cleaned Structure section shows either the framework or the removed solvent in a second viewer, with formula, atom count and solvent SMILES, which can be checked against the raw view above
Download Cleaned MOF saves the framework as <name>_gtsr.cif

steps.step: decide whether the result can be used
steps.here: Want to check stability? runs a stability model on the framework and reports stable or not stable

distinctive: Two model checkpoints: one removes only free solvent, the other removes all solvent including bound solvent. The choice is made before running.
A threshold for the probability that an atom is solvent controls how aggressively the structure is cleaned
After cleaning, a separate model predicts whether the framework stays stable once activated
The result is cleared if the uploaded file (checked by hash) or the checkpoint changes, and the person is asked to run it again
The removed solvent molecules are listed as SMILES strings

parts.title: Raw Structure
parts.summary: Takes the uploaded CIF and shows it in 3D with its formula and atom count, with display options.

parts.title: 3D crystal viewer with metrics
parts.summary: Draws a crystal structure in py3Dmol with a choice of style, element labels, the unit cell and rotation, along with metric cards for formula and atom count.

parts.title: Solvent removal controls
parts.summary: Picks the solvent model and threshold and runs the GNN cleaner, keeping the result tied to this input and model.

parts.title: Cleaned Structure
parts.summary: Shows the cleaned framework or the removed solvent with its SMILES, and offers the cleaned CIF for download.

parts.title: Activation Stability Prediction
parts.summary: Runs a stability model on the cleaned framework and reports whether it is stable.
